overview.summary: A Binary Search Tree (BST) is a tree where every left child is smaller than its parent, and every right child is greater.
learningObjectives: Implement BST search, insertion, and deletion.
Recognize that an in-order traversal of a BST yields sorted elements.
overview.interviewRelevance: BSTs combine the fast O(1) pointer updates of Linked Lists with the O(log N) fast search of Binary Search. They are extremely common.

paragraphs: Imagine looking for a word in a dictionary. You open to the middle. If your word is alphabetically earlier, you tear the book in half and throw away the back half. You repeat this until you find your word.
A BST enforces this 'dictionary' structure physically in memory, allowing you to discard half the tree with every step.
realWorldHook.ahaMoment: In a BST, every single node acts as a traffic cop pointing you left (smaller) or right (larger).

definition.technicalDefinition: A Binary Search Tree is a rooted binary tree data structure whose internal nodes each store a key greater than all the keys in the node's left subtree and less than those in its right subtree.

vocabulary.definition: Left Subtree < Node < Right Subtree for EVERY node.
Visiting Left, then Node, then Right. In a BST, this prints values in perfectly sorted order.
When the left and right subtrees have roughly the same height, ensuring O(log N) depth.

keyProperties: Average case O(log N) for Search, Insert, and Delete.
Worst case O(N) if the tree becomes unbalanced (like a straight line).

metaphor: A decision tree in a 'Guess Who' game. Each question eliminates a massive portion of the remaining candidates.
mentalModel.clickSentence: By strictly enforcing the rule 'Smaller to the left, Larger to the right', searching becomes a game of elimination.

memoryDescription: A BST uses the exact same TreeNode struct/class as a normal Binary Tree.
The magic is not in the memory structure, but in the strict rules applied when inserting data.

operations.name: Search
operations.description: Compare target with node. Go left if smaller, go right if larger.

code.python:
curr = root
while curr:
    if target == curr.val: return True
    elif target < curr.val: curr = curr.left
    else: curr = curr.right
return False

operations.visualNote: A pointer starts at root and slides down the correct path.

operations.name: Insertion
operations.description: Perform a search until you hit Null, then attach the new node there.
operations.visualNote: Traverse to an empty spot and spawn a new leaf.

patternTemplate.pseudocode:
def inorder(node):
  if not node: return
  inorder(node.left)
  process(node.val)
  inorder(node.right)
patternTemplate.whenToUse: When you need to maintain a dynamically changing dataset that requires fast lookups, insertions, and ordered iterations.
patternTemplate.timeComplexity: O(log N) for balanced trees, O(N) worst case.

recognitionQuiz.problemStatement: You need to store a stream of incoming numbers and frequently find the 'kth smallest' number seen so far.
recognitionQuiz.explanation: An array would require O(N) shifting to insert. A hash map doesn't maintain order. A BST (or Heap) inserts in O(log N) and an In-Order traversal easily finds the Kth smallest element.

examples.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
examples.problemStatement: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST).
steps: A node's value must not only be greater than its left child, but greater than EVERYTHING in its left subtree.
Pass a valid range (min, max) down the recursion.
For left children, update the max bound.
For right children, update the min bound.

code.python:
def isValidBST(root, min_val=float('-inf'), max_val=float('inf')):
    if not root: return True
    if not (min_val < root.val < max_val): return False
    return (isValidBST(root.left, min_val, root.val) and
            isValidBST(root.right, root.val, max_val))

examples.rationale: By carrying constraints downward, we ensure the strict BST invariant holds globally, not just locally.

conceptQuiz.question: What happens if you insert sorted data (e.g., 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) into a basic BST?
options: It degrades into a Linked List (O(N) search).
It stays perfectly balanced (O(log N) search).
conceptQuiz.explanation: Because every new number is larger, it always goes to the right, forming a straight line. (Advanced trees like AVL or Red-Black fix this by auto-balancing).

conceptQuiz.question: Which traversal prints a BST in perfectly sorted order?
conceptQuiz.explanation: In-Order visits the Left Subtree (smaller), then the Node (middle), then the Right Subtree (larger).

practice.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
practice.keyInsight: Pass a valid [min, max] range down to every node.

practice.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST
practice.keyInsight: If both targets are smaller, go left. If both are larger, go right. Otherwise, you are at the LCA.

practice.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
practice.keyInsight: An in-order traversal yields the k-th element naturally.

practice.title: Convert Sorted Array to Binary Search Tree
practice.keyInsight: The middle of the array is the root.
